content.title: Unit Rates: Speed and Density
content.overview: This lesson focuses on calculating and comparing two specific types of unit rates: speed (distance per time) and density (mass per volume). You will learn to compute these rates independently and then form ratios or quotients to compare them as required by ACT problems.
learning_objectives: Define and calculate speed as a unit rate of distance divided by time.
Define and calculate density as a unit rate of mass divided by volume.
Apply the Separate-Compute-Compare strategy to solve problems involving multiple unit rates.
Simplify numeric quotients formed by comparing speed and density.

sections.title: Understanding Speed and Density
sections.content: A unit rate describes how many units of the first quantity correspond to one unit of the second quantity. Speed is the unit rate of distance traveled over a specific duration of time (Speed = Distance ÷ Time). Common units include miles per hour (mph) or meters per second (m/s). Density is the unit rate of mass contained within a specific volume (Density = Mass ÷ Volume). Common units include kilograms per cubic meter (kg/m³) or grams per milliliter (g/mL).

sections.title: The Separate-Compute-Compare Strategy
sections.content:
When an ACT problem asks you to compare a speed to a density, follow these three steps: 1. Compute the speed unit rate by dividing the total distance by the total time. 2. Compute the density unit rate by dividing the total mass by the total volume. 3. Form the requested quotient or ratio using the two numeric results and simplify the fraction or decimal.

![A flowchart showing the steps to compare speed and density: first calculate speed, then calculate density, then divide speed by density.](https://img.justsolvely.com/followUpImage/3d96721f-5484-4f3a-9377-ce9e7d754e28-1786505523390-921.webp)

worked_examples.question: A delivery van travels 240 miles in 4 hours. It carries a crate with a mass of 1,200 kg and a volume of 2 cubic meters. What is the ratio of the van's speed to the crate's density?
worked_examples.solution: Step 1: Compute the speed. Speed = 240 miles ÷ 4 hours = 60 miles per hour. Step 2: Compute the density. Density = 1,200 kg ÷ 2 m³ = 600 kg/m³. Step 3: Form the ratio of speed to density. Ratio = 60 / 600. Step 4: Simplify the fraction. 60/600 = 6/60 = 1/10 or 0.1.

common_mistakes: Attempting to combine all four numbers (distance, time, mass, volume) into one large fraction immediately, which often leads to inversion errors.
Confusing the formulas for speed and density (e.g., dividing time by distance).
Misplacing decimal points when converting a simplified fraction into a decimal value.
exam_tips: Always calculate the individual unit rates first before trying to compare them.
Pay close attention to the order of the comparison; 'speed to density' means speed is the numerator and density is the denominator.
Units in these specific ACT problems often do not cancel out; focus on the numeric values requested by the answer choices.
content.recap: To compare speed and density, calculate each as a unit rate (Distance/Time and Mass/Volume) and then divide the resulting numbers to find the final ratio.

knowledge_claims.content: Speed is defined as the unit rate of distance divided by time.
Density is defined as the unit rate of mass divided by volume.
The formula for calculating a speed unit rate is Speed = Distance ÷ Time.
The formula for calculating a density unit rate is Density = Mass ÷ Volume.
The Separate-Compute-Compare strategy requires calculating individual unit rates before forming a final comparison quotient.
In a ratio of 'A to B', the value for A serves as the numerator and the value for B serves as the denominator.
Units such as miles per hour (mph) indicate a speed rate, while units such as kg/m³ indicate a density rate.
A common error is dividing time by distance instead of distance by time when calculating speed.
A common error is dividing volume by mass instead of mass by volume when calculating density.
After calculating a ratio of two rates, verify the numeric simplification by converting the fraction to a decimal if necessary.
If a truck travels 360 miles in 4.5 hours, its unit rate of speed is 80 miles per hour.
If cargo has a mass of 2700 kg and a volume of 3.0 m³, its unit rate of density is 900 kg per m³.

items.stem:
Practice form 1.
A cyclist travels 12 miles in 2 hours. What is the average speed?
A) 6 miles per hour
B) 12 miles per hour
C) 3 miles per hour
D) 5 miles per hour
items.explanation: Average speed equals distance divided by time.

items.stem:
Practice form 2.
A cyclist travels 24 miles in 3 hours. What is the average speed?
A) 24 miles per hour
B) 4 miles per hour
C) 8 miles per hour
D) 7 miles per hour
items.explanation: Average speed equals distance divided by time.
